identityReview: Ilham Aliyev / İlham Əliyev, born 24 December 1961 in Baku; distinguish from his father Heydar Aliyev and wife Mehriban Aliyeva. Official biography supports SOCAR vice-presidential service, parliamentary and short prime-ministerial service, presidency since 2003 and New Azerbaijan Party chairmanship since 2005. The 2024 election begins a fifth presidential term. Both governments’ November 2026 meeting records identify him as Azerbaijan’s president. Do not substitute his wife’s offices or his father’s career for his own, or call SOCAR vice-presidency company presidency.
lifeStatusEvidence: Armenia’s prime minister and Azerbaijan’s presidency both report that Aliyev met Nikol Pashinyan in Dublin on 12 November 2026 at the European Political Community summit. This is a completed-event record, not a planned invitation or undated current-profile assertion. No photographs or video were visually reviewed.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read official biography, concise RFE/RL inauguration account, relevant 2017 appointment passages, all nine 2020 ceasefire provisions, selected 2023 ICJ-summary passages and operative clauses, OSCE 2024 press findings, relevant 2024 inauguration passages, HRW introduction/media section, 2026 joint anniversary statement and both November meeting releases. Library of Congress constitutional history and UNHCR arrival figures were checked through indexed excerpts because original bodies returned 403/429. Read portrait licence/metadata and the presidency’s reuse terms, without image pixels.
corrections: Read the official biography’s birth, education and career chronology. It gives 24 December 1961 in Baku, MGIMO study in 1977–1982, postgraduate work, history thesis in 1985 and teaching until 1990; these are biographical statements, not inspected university records. SOCAR vice-president and first vice-president roles cover 1994–August 2003, without a separate first-vice-president promotion date. Do not call him SOCAR president. Parliament elections in 1995 and 2000, premiership on 4 August 2003 and party chairmanship in 2005 are separated. The five presidential election dates support fifth-term chronology; official vote percentages are not independent electoral-quality findings and are omitted.

Read the short contemporaneous RFE/RL inauguration report dated 31 October 2003. It explicitly says he was inaugurated that day, succeeded his father Heydar/Heidar Aliyev, and followed the widely criticized 15 October election. The election date, inauguration date and short preceding premiership are distinct. The article attributes the vote tally to election officials; the dossier does not independently endorse that percentage or infer a court judgment invalidating the election.

Read indexed Library of Congress Global Legal Monitor excerpts of the 24 March 2017 article. They explicitly identify the 21 February appointment of his wife, new constitutional article 103(1), September 2016 creation of vice-presidential offices and extension of the presidential term from five to seven years. The body returned 403, so no full-article or underlying constitutional-text audit is claimed. Presidential term length and removal of limits on the number of terms are different changes; no claim that term limits were abolished in 2016 is made. March publication is not the appointment date.

Read the 21 February 2017 official Security Council meeting account, especially the announcement and introductory biographical passages. It records the president’s appointment of Mehriban Aliyeva that day and her previous parliamentary and Heydar Aliyev Foundation roles. His praise of her competence and claimed programme successes is political speech, not an independent appraisal. This is a historical appointment, not an assumption about every later office or an attribution of his wife’s achievements to him.

Read the nine operative provisions of the 10 November 2020 tripartite statement published by the Azerbaijani presidency. They specify a ceasefire from 00:00 Moscow time that day, territorial-transfer arrangements, Russian peacekeepers, displaced persons, exchanges and transport links. The original text’s planned dates and renewable peacekeeper term are historical provisions, not proof of their later fulfillment or continuing deployment in November 2026. No assertion that the statement permanently resolved all disputes, completed all returns or constituted the later peace treaty is made.

Read the indexed UNHCR Armenia response overview, which explicitly places over 100000 arrivals within one week in September 2023. The UNHCR Japan 6 October 2023 indexed release connects the exodus to Azerbaijani military operations. Opening both pages and the emergency-requirements PDF returned 429, so their full bodies were not reviewed. The 19 September operation date is corroborated in the ICJ summary. Do not substitute later total refugee stocks for this one-week flow or infer that every displaced person’s property claim has been adjudicated.

Read selected background, rights/plausibility, provisional-measures and operative-clause passages of the Court’s summary of the 17 November 2023 order. The document distinguishes Armenia’s requested measures and allegations from the Court’s actual orders. Operative paragraphs cover safe return and departure, protection from force or intimidation, preservation and consideration of identity/property records, and an eight-week reporting obligation. These are provisional measures under CERD, not a final merits ruling, a genocide finding or a criminal conviction of Aliyev. Do not replace the actual reporting period with the applicant’s requested one-month/quarterly schedule. The full underlying order, later case developments and every dissent were not reviewed.

Read the 8 February 2024 ODIHR/OSCE PA statement concerning the previous day’s early presidential election. It credits efficient preparations while identifying absent genuine pluralism, restrictions on critical voices, noncompetitive alternatives and serious polling/counting safeguards problems. These are attributed observer findings, not a judicial annulment or a statement about the separate September 2024 parliamentary election. The presence of six other candidates does not establish effective competition. No full final observation report or precinct-level dataset was audited.

Read the date, opening inauguration account, Constitutional Court confirmation passage and oath sequence of the official 14 February 2024 report. It records the completed ceremony at the Milli Majlis, following the 7 February election and 13 February confirmation. It is not an advance invitation. The president’s subsequent claims about achievements and support are his speech, not adopted as independent facts; the whole lengthy speech and videos were not reviewed.

Read World Report 2026’s Azerbaijan introduction and freedom-of-expression/media passages. The chapter explicitly reviews events of 2025 and criticizes repression of media, opposition and civil society. The dossier attributes these assessments to HRW and does not relabel them as a complete November 2026 conditions audit or individual judicial verdicts. Specific journalists’ later case outcomes were not checked and are not presented as current custody facts. Its broad description of the Washington process is distinguished from the primary statement’s more precise declaration-versus-initialed-draft terminology.

Read the 10 August 2026 US-Armenia-Azerbaijan anniversary statement published by the Armenian foreign ministry, including its explicit account of the 2025 White House summit. Aliyev and Pashinyan signed the joint declaration; the foreign ministers initialed the draft peace and interstate-relations agreement. August 8 is independently specified in both November meeting accounts. Political claims about ending conflict and infrastructure progress do not establish treaty ratification, completed construction or independently audited trade totals. A Nobel nomination is not an award; the nomination and financial/trade figures are not imported into the biography.

Read the Armenian prime minister’s 12 November 2026 Dublin meeting release. It records an actual meeting with Aliyev at the ninth European Political Community summit and discussion of peace, transport, trade and border delimitation. The forthcoming electricity-grid interconnection is a prospective matter. Cargo totals are official claims rather than independent audit results and are omitted. This supplies recent activity evidence; it does not announce ratification or entry into force of the full peace agreement.

Read the Azerbaijani presidency’s corresponding 12 November 2026 Dublin meeting account. It corroborates the participants and event, and describes TRIPP railway/highway planning and design, prospects for connectivity, future grid links and transboundary-water cooperation. These are not proof that every construction project is complete, that Armenian sovereignty was transferred, or that all disputed legal questions are settled. The two government accounts agree on the meeting but remain official reports; no image pixels, recording or independent cargo dataset was inspected.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified native-language human review. No birth or university certificate, full constitutional text, raw election results, complete observation report, full ICJ docket, individual human-rights case files, construction audit, trade dataset, event recording or portrait pixels were reviewed. Keep allegations, observer findings, interim orders, political declarations and legally completed treaty steps distinct. Refresh current roles, treaty status and later rights developments before publication.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages checked against Chinese and English. Preserve birth and education dates; parliament, premiership and presidency distinctions; father/wife identity; SOCAR vice-president versus president; 2016 term length versus term-count limits; 2017 appointed office; 2020 provisions versus fulfillment; September 2023 one-week arrivals versus later refugee stocks; ICJ interim measures versus merits/criminal judgment; February 2024 presidential election versus parliamentary election; fifth term versus election day/inauguration; 2025 signed declaration versus initialed draft treaty; 2026 HRW publication versus 2025 events; November Dublin meeting and future infrastructure plans.
